core.title: Extract all refinement fields when refining ambiguous input into a wagon
core.given: A planner holds ambiguous input (possibly free-form) that must become a structured wagon definition (the plan artifact defining one bounded slice of the product).
core.when: Refining that input into a wagon definition.
core.then: Extract subject, action, goal, context, outcome, produce, consume and theme into the wagon definition.
prefer: subject: WHO/WHAT performs the action (actor:role or entity:state).
produce: owned output artifacts; consume: input artifacts owned by other wagons.

theme: one of mechanic, scenario, match, sensory, player, league, audience, monetization, partnership, commons — pick the one whose scope matches: mechanic = Core game rules, decision systems, and immediate feedback loops; scenario = Content ingestion, entity extraction, and narrative structure processing; match = Session orchestration, state management, and lifecycle control, Multi-player coordination, turn management; sensory = UI rendering, audio mixing, gesture capture, and player interaction; player = Individual lifecycle, onboarding, progression, and session management; league = Competitive organization, bracket management, and tournament operations; audience = Spectator engagement, streaming infrastructure, and viewer participation; monetization = Token economy, wallet operations, and transaction processing; partnership = Sponsor/partner onboarding, delegation, and commercial integration; commons = Shared infrastructure, cross-cutting utilities, and platform services.
avoid: Non-present-tense actions; goals with several intents; unmeasurable outcomes.
Other wagons' artifacts under produce, or own artifacts under consume.
Themes outside the taxonomy; descriptions under 10 characters.
core.why: Structured fields make the wagon's intent, scope, ownership and success checkable; later coherence checks validate exactly these fields.
evidence: Wagon definition contains subject, action, goal, context, outcome, produce, consume and theme fields.
subject matches actor:role or entity:state; context is comma-separated conditions; theme is a member of the canonical theme taxonomy.
Every produce artifact is owned by this wagon; every consume artifact is owned by another wagon.
verification: Check the refined wagon definition against the full field map: subject = WHO/WHAT performs the action (actor:role or entity:state); action = core present-tense verb phrase; goal = WHY/motivation, single intent statement; context = WHEN/WHERE, comma-separated conditions; outcome = measurable progress/result statement; produce = owned output artifacts; consume = input artifacts owned by other wagons.

Validate theme against the canonical theme taxonomy and its scope definitions (allowed values and scopes: mechanic = Core game rules, decision systems, and immediate feedback loops; scenario = Content ingestion, entity extraction, and narrative structure processing; match = Session orchestration, state management, and lifecycle control, Multi-player coordination, turn management; sensory = UI rendering, audio mixing, gesture capture, and player interaction; player = Individual lifecycle, onboarding, progression, and session management; league = Competitive organization, bracket management, and tournament operations; audience = Spectator engagement, streaming infrastructure, and viewer participation; monetization = Token economy, wallet operations, and transaction processing; partnership = Sponsor/partner onboarding, delegation, and commercial integration; commons = Shared infrastructure, cross-cutting utilities, and platform services).

Activation is keyed on the task term and fires only for refinement of genuinely ambiguous input (unclear subject, intent, scope, ownership or success): free-form or unstructured format is only one possible form of ambiguous input and never qualifies on its own; presence or absence of acceptance criteria does not decide ambiguity; bare terms like 'wagon' are not sufficient; the file-kind and change facts are candidate signals only and never establish refinement of ambiguous input by themselves.

fires: Planner turns an ambiguous feature request or idea (unclear who acts, why, or what counts as done) into a new structured wagon definition
Planner is asked to refine a vague wagon draft whose intent, scope or artifact ownership is ambiguous into its structured fields
doesNotFire: Input is already clear and unambiguous, even if written as free-form prose
Planner edits a single field (e.g. theme only) of an already-refined wagon without refining new ambiguous input
Coder implements code inside an already-refined wagon
Documentation-only edits that do not refine input into a wagon

neutralityNotes: This is a planner-process rule over product-domain artifacts, so it is almost entirely stack-neutral already. 'wagon' and 'wagon manifest' are the product's names for a bounded slice of the product and its definition artifact (cf. layout.wagon_dir and urn.wagon in the profile vocabulary), not stack terms, so they stay in the core. The theme taxonomy with all ten theme-to-scope definitions from the sidecar's shared node is product-domain data identical across stacks; it is preserved inline and verbatim in the core (prefer[6] and the theme-validation verification entry) rather than becoming a profile key, because no vocabulary group covers domain taxonomies and a profile key would have to be per-stack, which this data is not; only the shared-node locator itself is bunOnly. bun.json states no paths, suffixes, URNs, runners or other structure values that the core must consume, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The only realization-specific content is that shared taxonomy-node locator (prefer[6], verifier_detail[2]) and the sidecar term ids (verifier_detail[3]), kept in bunOnly. The activation fact notes could not be carried verbatim because the neutral core's fact schema has no note field; their qualifying content (decisive vs candidate signals; input format and presence/absence of acceptance criteria do not decide activation) is preserved in the core's verification array and doesNotFire, so no condition was dropped.
